entities.summary: A compact Šumava circuit linking two contrasting glacial lakes beneath steep cirque walls.

names.local: Jizerskohorské bučiny – Oldřichovský Špičák a Skalní hrad

entities.summary: A steep old-beech-forest circuit through granite boulders, crags and the UNESCO-listed Jizera Mountains beech landscape, with an exceptional autumn transformation.
entities.description: The loop from Oldřichov v Hájích climbs through the Jizerskohorské bučiny toward Skalní hrad and Oldřichovský Špičák. Unlike the broad plateau routes elsewhere in the Jizera Mountains, this side is steep, enclosed and rocky: roots, granite blocks, steps and short ladder-like passages sit inside mature beech forest. In the national nature reserve visitors must remain on designated paths.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Already A/D2 in ordinary season; at peak beech colour the combination of old forest, steep relief, granite and low autumn light can reach S-like experiential quality and D4 drive-worthiness. It is one of the few Czech seasonal transformations worth structuring a weekend around.

names.local: Labský důl – Pančavský vodopád – Pramen Labe

entities.summary: A long glacial-valley ascent to the Krkonoše tundra plateau, linking Labský důl, the source of the Labe and Pančavský vodopád.
entities.description: The lower route follows the deepening Labský důl before climbing to Labská bouda and the plateau. Pančavský vodopád is encountered in the context of its hanging valley rather than as an isolated viewpoint. Snow can linger high above a green valley, and cloud or wind can remove much of the upper-route appeal.
entities.whyWorthwhile: A complete glacial-valley-to-tundra day with strong geomorphology throughout the climb.

entities.summary: A point-to-point route through both Ostaš sandstone labyrinths, then down toward the unusual sandstone columns at Česká Metuje.
